verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_fibonacci_polyglot: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Function names are clear (bigint_add, print_fib), but the language-switching trick (`#if 0` / `r""" # "`) has no comment explaining it; the only comment is "# Python implementation below". Single-letter names a, b, t and a vague `temp` are used in business logic.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Functions are short, but the code adds an unneeded bignum (BASE, MAX_LIMBS=50000) where the convention asks for a clear iterative Fibonacci. It also uses two switching mechanisms: the Python block sits inside a string AND inside `#if 0`. A compiled cmain binary was left in the diff.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No input validation in C: `if (argc < 2) return 0;`, and `atoll` accepts garbage. Python exits 0 silently when no argument is given. There is no bounds check on `limbs[MAX_LIMBS]`, so a large n overflows the buffer. Negative n silently prints 0.

items.name: Boundary and large inputs
items.evidence: f(0)=0, f(1)=1 and large n are correct and iterative in both languages, and outputs matched up to n=10000. But missing args exit 0 with no output, and negative or non-numeric input prints 0 instead of exiting non-zero.

items.name: Exact invocation contract
items.evidence: Works with both exact commands and compiles cleanly even with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic. However, the agent recompiled at the end, so polyglot/cmain was left next to the 'single file'. That is a likely cause of the hidden test_fibonacci_polyglot failure.
